beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact thought process repeatedly reads and updates it before reconstruction.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: ThinkSR separates the spatial carrier from the compact computation that works on it. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. Windowing gives the thought process local groups of tokens. DQ-CTM runs recurrent ticks with shared parameters. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into a super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR runs dense features through compact recurrent thought
params.note: The recurrence returns to the thought stage, not the whole flow.

beats.intent: The carrier equation makes the dense feature field first, then partitions that field into windows without dropping tokens.
beats.narration: The carrier is defined before the compact thought process acts on it. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the dense feature field. The window partition acts on that field and preserves the tokens as windowed input.

params.headline: The carrier stays dense before windowed thought begins

terms.label: window partition that keeps every token

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the benchmark; its 1.129 million parameters are second largest among the five methods.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison runs from the smallest model to the largest. CATANet and RFDN are both below six tenths of a million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is the largest model in this table.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is second largest by parameter count
